evals.prompt: Add a `formatCurrency(amount, currency)` helper to `src/utils/money.ts` and use it in the new invoice screen.
evals.expected_output: Searches the codebase for existing implementations before writing anything — by name, keyword, and string literal — because a currency formatter is the kind of thing that already exists once or twice. Reuses or extends the existing one rather than adding a near-duplicate, and reports any duplicates found as a finding.

evals.prompt: Add a webhook endpoint that marks a subscription as cancelled when the billing provider calls us.
evals.expected_output: Locates the real code path from the true entry point and records the call chain as file:line hops, reads every file it intends to change completely, finds all callers of anything it modifies, and identifies the contracts it must not break — route surface, persisted schema, and event shape. Plans before coding and covers failure paths (retries, duplicate delivery, out-of-order events).

evals.prompt: We're migrating from the old `UserRepo` to the new `UserRepository`. I've moved the three call sites in the auth module. Good to merge?
evals.expected_output: Flags the risk specific to refactors: a half-migrated state that leaves two ways to do one thing permanently. Requires a full sweep for remaining references — including dynamic ones — and either completing the migration or deleting the old implementation, rather than leaving both alive.

evals.prompt: I added the `NotificationService` class and its tests pass. Feature done?
evals.expected_output: Rejects passing unit tests as proof the feature works, and requires tracing the end-to-end path in the modified code to confirm the wiring is real — imports resolved, provider registered, dependency injected, route or subscriber actually reachable from the entry point. Names code-that-exists-but-is-not-wired-in as a common silent failure in agent-written changes.

evals.prompt: Make the dashboard load faster — it's sluggish with a lot of records.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to optimize without measurement first, identifying the actual hot path rather than guessing. Looks for algorithmic traps and N+1 query patterns, establishes a baseline, and verifies the improvement by measurement rather than by inspection.

evals.prompt: Rename `getUser` to `fetchUser` across the repo and also switch it to return null instead of throwing when the user is missing.
evals.expected_output: Separates the mechanical rename from the behavior change rather than shipping them together, because a rename mixed with a contract change is unreviewable. Enumerates every caller and checks which ones relied on the throw, and treats the null-vs-throw switch as a contract change with its own blast radius and tests.

evals.prompt: Here's my plan: I'll add a `retryWithBackoff` wrapper in the orders service. Start coding.
evals.expected_output: Produces the written plan first — understanding, root cause or gap, approach, changes, reuse, risk and blast radius, verification, and out-of-scope findings — rather than coding straight from the user's proposal. Checks whether a retry helper already exists and whether the orders service is the right layer to own retry semantics, or whether that belongs in the adapter for the external system.

evals.prompt: Small change: the CSV export is missing the header row. Just add it.
evals.expected_output: Treats the small change with the same discipline — reads the real code path, and performs the mandatory pattern sweep across the codebase rather than assuming a one-line edit is contained. Checks whether other export paths share the defect and whether any consumer parses the file positionally and would break when a header appears.
